news.title: Anthropic招股书大篇幅提示AI投资风险，却淡化社会风险
news.snippet: 学者在《财富》撰文指出，Anthropic的IPO文件用近七万字详述AI投资者风险，却几乎未谈社会影响。
news.raw_snippet:
In his latest Fortune article, Bhaskar Chakravorti, Dean of Global Business at The Fletcher School and Chair of Digital Planet, argues that Anthropic’s IPO filing extensively details the financial risks of artificial intelligence to investors while giving far less attention to the potential harm AI poses to workers, consumers, and society. [...] His central argument is that AI companies must look beyond shareholder interests and recognize that the social costs of AI may eventually become financial liabilities. Greater transparency and accountability, he suggests, are essential to ensuring that AI’s economic benefits do not come at the expense of the broader public.

news.title: 人工智能时代的网络安全之变
news.snippet: AI正重塑网络安全格局，在提升智能防御的同时扩大攻击面，企业须更新安全策略以应对新型威胁与合规风险。
news.raw_snippet:
Something else to keep in mind when it comes to AI is the kind of information you feed it.

“If you wouldn't post it publicly or email it to a stranger, don't paste it into an AI prompt,” said John Virden, chief information security officer for Miami. [...] One of the oldest scams in the book involves scammers calling a person to ask for money or information, often while impersonating a loved one or authority figure. Well, scammers can’t be bothered to make their own phone calls anymore – now they’re using AI to do it. [...] Try to pinpoint phishing based on other clues, including:

 Making sure the “from” address is a known sender
 Hovering over any links to ensure they go to real websites
 Treating requests for money, personal information, or favors with great suspicion

It would be easier if the bad actors stuck to the old ways. They are unfortunately changing with the times, and we have to change with them in order to remain a step ahead.

news.title: 生成式AI时代创作权的心理价值
news.snippet: 研究表明，尽管生成式AI可快速产出内容，人类创作者身份仍对自我价值、认同感与心理健康具有重要意义。
news.raw_snippet: While generative artificial intelligence (AI) can quickly produce appealing work, human involvement in creation may still matter to creators themselves, audiences and those who assign credit. This review examines research across creative, communicative and service domains, including art, literature, music, science, marketing and advice. We organize the evidence by evaluator, by the outcome measured and its timing, and by what was compared, including differences in content, in information about [...] identity, and skills. A well-rated result does not reveal the value of a particular human contribution or the consequences of delegating it to AI. Nor is more human involvement automatically better. Choosing to delegate work or selected work tasks to AI can itself express agency. As AI agents become capable of taking on more creative processes, deciding what to delegate may become a central form of human involvement. This review offers a framework for identifying which contributions matter to [...] of ownership. The strongest evidence concerns origin-information effects, where labeling the same work as human-versus AI-made can change immediate evaluator ratings. In blinded studies, AI-generated texts were rated higher than human-written texts, yet labeling the text as AI-generated lowered its ratings.
